defs.Electric charge: A property of matter, positive or negative, that makes objects push or pull on each other.
defs.Coulomb's law: How strongly two charges push or pull: more charge, more force; twice as far, a quarter of the force.
defs.Superposition: With many charges, the force on one is the sum of the pushes and pulls from each of the others.
defs.Electric field: The push a charge would feel at each point in space, per unit of charge.
defs.Gauss's law: The total field coming out of any closed surface depends only on the charge inside it.
defs.Voltage: Energy per unit of charge: how much work moving a charge from one point to another takes or gives.
defs.Conductor: A material, like copper, in which some charges are free to move.
defs.Current: The rate at which charge flows past a point.
defs.Resistance: How much a material opposes current, turning the energy into heat.
defs.Capacitance: How much charge two separated conductors hold for a given voltage; energy stored in the electric field.
defs.Inductance: How strongly a coil opposes changes in its current; energy stored in the magnetic field.
defs.Magnetic field: The field made by moving charges and currents, which pushes on other moving charges.
defs.Induction: A changing magnetic field drives a voltage around a loop; how generators and transformers work.
defs.Maxwell's equations: The four laws that together describe all electric and magnetic fields, including light.
defs.Energy flow: Where electrical energy actually travels: through the fields around wires, not inside the metal.
defs.Circuit laws: Kirchhoff's rules for currents and voltages in circuits, valid when signals change slowly.
